root_idea.summary: The root centers on forceful pushing, driving, or repelling.
root_idea.development: From forceful دفع, the lexical field extends to thrusting or piercing, driving in fasteners, and propelling or opposing water. Related terms describe strength, forceful advance, or a troop that presses against an enemy, while the ship-fastening noun is treated as a specialized branch.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular citation form دِسَار; the Quran attests its plural دُسُر.

senses.definition: A nail used to fasten the planks of a ship; collectively, ship’s nails.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural دُسُر is used in the description of Noah’s vessel. This is the interpretation supported by the supplied Quran-focused gloss.

senses.definition: A binding cord made from palm fibres, used to join and fasten a ship’s planks.
senses.usage_conditions: A reported alternative interpretation of the Quranic plural دُسُر in the Noah-vessel construction; the supplied lexical evidence records the passage as referring either to nails or to such cords.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To push, thrust, drive, propel, or repel someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes a thing driven by the sea onto the shore and a ship repelling or opposing water with its prow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To thrust, pierce, or stab forcefully with a spear.
To drive in a nail; to nail, fasten, or repair a ship by joining its planks with nails or palm-fibre cord.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes fastening or repairing a ship, including joining its planks in a sewing-like manner.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ship characterized by repelling or opposing water with its prow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal usage associated with the action of pushing back water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bulky, strong, vigorous, or spirited camel; also, something characterized as strong and spirited.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a large or powerful camel, including a she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tough, hardy lion, firm in build.
An army, troop of horse, or portion of an army gathered as a compact force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a collected military body or troop.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who thrusts repeatedly or vigorously with a spear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An agent-noun usage derived from forceful spear-thrusting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who frequently has sexual intercourse.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Forceful pushing, driving, propelling, and repelling.
Driving nails and fastening or repairing ship planks.
Specialized ship term describing opposition to water.
Quran-attested noun interpreted as ship nails or palm-fibre binding cords.
Bulky, strong, or vigorous camel usage.
Agent noun for repeated or vigorous spear-thrusting.

cautions: The Quranic plural دُسُر in 54:13 has two reported lexical interpretations in the supplied evidence: ship’s nails or palm-fibre binding cords. The supplied contextual gloss is “and nails.”
